outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: new held_and_measured(ctx, run_id) reads the recorded runs once and returns (row, measured, why). The measured row comes from _evio.measured_row, so for a repeat it is the run its reusedFrom names. A repeat whose source the ledger does not hold is refused with 'run X repeated the verdict of run Y, which the ledger does not hold: a repeat whose source is gone names no tree'. gate_binding now reads steps, coverage and testedState.head off the measured row. It requires both rows to be passed, and checks the measured row's head against proof['head'] with _evio.same_head (a new refusal). It returns the measured run's id, so fixLegRunId names the run that measured. The clause adds ' as run <held>, which repeated its verdict' when the held green was a repeat; refusals read off the measured row name both ids. A part-reused row is still its own measured row, so a copied step stays refused by step_standing. gate_binding's docstring is rewritten. tests/test_drive_phase.py: fbr1-fbr5 (_fix_by_gate_repeat_units, ux-block) build the repeat the way it reads back: the source's steps copied and marked reusedFrom, no coverage, empty testedState. That shape came from dumping real rows: the read-back repeat carries the copied steps marked, not `steps: []` as the task text says. fbr6 (_fix_by_gate_repeat_real_cases, new stage fbr-block) runs the real run-test-gate.py --task P1.1 --record twice on a tdd fixture with a pytest-shaped suite, then calls gate_binding against the real ledger with the repeat held. The existing filed_over and fbm green_row fixtures gained testedState.head 'abc1234' (the proof's head) so they stay bound under the head check. filed_over takes a ledger= argument for rows beside the held one.
